{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZWUS4Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC9psI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 25, "title": "Implement WRAM-to-$2180 conflict suppression for DMA and HDMA", "body": "## Problem

DMA and HDMA currently copy WRAM through the B-bus WMDATA port as ordinary transfers. The shared `SystemBus::transfer` path checks A-bus register exclusions but never checks whether its A endpoint is WRAM while its effective B endpoint is `$2180`. Consequently, `write_raw($2180, value)` writes memory and advances the WRAM-port pointer.

This is the next incomplete behavior identified by the supplied latest assessment. It also requires correcting an existing test contract: `dma_progression_rechecks_each_byte_and_wraps_without_bank_carry` expects `$80:0000` mirrored WRAM to copy through `$2180` after an A-address wrap. Preserve its address-wrap coverage while replacing the unsupported successful-copy expectation.

Evidence at baseline `af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e`:

- [Shared transfer path](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L431): ordinary B-bus writes without conflict detection.
- [WRAM decoding and WMDATA writes](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L312): WRAM banks/mirrors and unconditional port increment.
- [Contradictory wraparound vectors](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/crates/snes-core/src/machine/dma_tests.rs#L190).
- [Remaining DMA/HDMA limitations](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/docs/issue-23-validation.md#remaining-scope).

The supplied open-Issue list is empty; this behavior was explicitly excluded from Issues #21 and #23.

## Expected outcome

Implement forward, A-to-B WRAM/WMDATA conflict handling in the shared DMA/HDMA payload path.

The precise implementation target, subject to the mandatory specification check below, is:

1. Classify the actual A address for each payload byte as WRAM when it is in `$7E:0000–$7F:FFFF`, or `$0000–$1FFF` in banks `$00–$3F/$80–$BF`.
2. Resolve the effective B register using the channel's transfer-mode offset and eight-bit BBAD wrapping. Suppress the WMDATA write only when that register is `$2180` and the A source is WRAM.
3. A conflicting byte copies no data through WMDATA and does not increment its 17-bit pointer. The transfer still consumes its byte slot and retains normal DMA address/count progression or HDMA payload-pointer/line progression.
4. Apply the same payload rule to general DMA, direct HDMA and indirect HDMA. Indirect HDMA uses its payload bank/address, not the table bank, for this decision.
5. Retain legal ROM/SRAM-to-WMDATA transfers, WRAM-to-other-B-register transfers, CPU WMDATA accesses and HDMA descriptor/indirect-pointer fetches.

**Specification prerequisite:** consult [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), sections `2180 WMDATA`, `43x0 DMAPx`, and `DMA AND HDMA`; cross-check [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), WRAM-port, memory-map and DMA/HDMA sections. Record the exact passages supporting the no-copy, no-port-increment and continued-progression rules before treating them as hardware expectations. Correct any proposed assertion that those passages contradict.

These are specification links already identified by repository documentation. Their conflict passages were unavailable locally and were not fetched during this repository-only evaluation. In particular, this Issue does **not** establish that reverse `$2180`-to-WRAM conflicts write zero, preserve memory, or have any particular electrical bus value. That direction remains explicitly unresolved and outside this bounded implementation.

Scope excludes reverse conflict implementation, electrical/open-bus accuracy, DMA startup/alignment changes, HDMA initialization/overhead/first-frame corrections, same-channel contention and unrelated I/O restrictions. Do not generalize the conflict to all WRAM accesses or all `$218x` registers.

## Context and reproduction

Create an original unit vector with WRAM source `$7E:0100 = $5A`, WMDATA pointer `$11000`, destination sentinel `$A6`, and a one-byte forward mode-0 DMA to BBAD `$80`.

Source inspection predicts the baseline changes the destination to `$5A` and advances the pointer to `$11001`. The intended correction preserves `$A6` and `$11000`, while advancing the DMA A address to `$0101`, retaining bank `$7E`, and completing the count. This prediction has not been executed by this evaluator.

The existing original [DMA guests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/crates/snes-core/tests/dma_access.rs) test a different case: prohibited **A-bus register** access at `$00:2180`. Preserve those tests and Issue #23's accessible `$4210–$421F` reads and acknowledgement coverage.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Document the specification passages and their applicability to DMA/direct HDMA/indirect HDMA. Distinguish documented semantics, retained timing conventions and unresolved reverse/electrical behavior; do not derive hardware requirements from existing test expectations.
- [ ] Implement the forward conflict in the shared payload path, with independent literal test expectations rather than expectations calculated by the production predicate.
- [ ] Cover both full WRAM banks and mirrored-bank boundaries `$00/$3F/$80/$BF`, including mirror offsets `$0000/$1FFF`. Include non-WRAM controls at `$2000` and banks `$40/$C0`, asserting only supported values and side effects.
- [ ] Exercise fixed, incrementing and decrementing DMA sources; A-address `$FFFF/$0000` wrapping without bank carry; entry into and exit from mirrored WRAM; and a multi-register B pattern that includes `$2180` and an ordinary neighboring register. Check destination sentinels, port pointer, final A address/bank/count and retained elapsed clocks. A conflict must neither terminate nor skip byte accounting. Include the zero-count/65,536-byte convention without claiming setup timing accuracy.
- [ ] Exercise complete direct and indirect HDMA tables with conflicting payloads, repeated rows and termination. Check payload/table/indirect-pointer advancement, line counters and active masks. Include a WRAM table with legal ROM payload and a ROM table with conflicting WRAM payload to distinguish table fetches from payload decisions.
- [ ] Preserve legal transfers in both directions, CPU WMDATA reads/writes including pointer wrapping, existing A-bus exclusions, status-register acknowledgement, deferred NMI, access-boundary timing and HDMA-preemption regressions. Correct only the conflicting forward wraparound expectations; retain their legal portions and progression assertions.
- [ ] Add an original source-built 65C816 guest that initializes memory and registers through CPU instructions, triggers conflicting DMA plus a legal control, and records numeric results in CPU-visible WRAM. Enforce instruction/frame deadlines and assert results independently. Record original MIT provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.
- [ ] Show new focused regressions failing on the unchanged baseline and passing with the implementation. Run `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::dma_tests` and `cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dma_access`.
- [ ] Pass the existing pre-merge gates from [README](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/README.md#validate) and [CI](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/af6b37d81a024a8d5c2d9255863321b751f5470e/.github/workflows/ci.yml):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Use README's documented compiler selection where required. Preserve source pins, provenance, cleared-game hashes, both 18,100-frame replays, Castle's complete route/credits, Memory audio assertions and all negative controls; do not shorten or weaken them.

- [ ] Update README and validation evidence with actual commands/results and remaining limitations. DMA and HDMA remain partial, including reverse conflicts and the excluded timing/matrix work. Preserve all 24 inventory scopes: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing` remain partial; `dsp-voices` remains implemented_unverified; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster`, `pal` remain unimplemented. Limited passes establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

None.
